title: Linearization of a right adjoint
statement:
Let $\pi$ be a projection formula for $P\colon\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ relative to a strong
monoidal $S\colon\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ ([def-sfb-projection-formula]). Let
$P\dashv G$ be an adjunction with counit $c$. Let
$$
\theta_{L,N}\colon SL\otimes GN\to G(L\otimes N)
$$
be the adjoint of
$P(SL\otimes GN)\xrightarrow{\pi_{L,GN}}L\otimes PGN\xrightarrow{L\otimes c_N}L\otimes N$.
Let $\mathcal B$ be a monoid object of $\mathcal D$. For a $\mathcal B$-module object $N$
([sk-def-sfb-module-objects]), the morphism
$$
S\mathcal B\otimes GN\xrightarrow{\theta_{\mathcal B,N}}G(\mathcal B\otimes N)
\xrightarrow{G\gamma_N}GN
$$
makes $GN$ an $S\mathcal B$-module object, and $Gf$ is $S\mathcal B$-linear for every
$\mathcal B$-linear $f$. This defines the *linearization*
$$
G_{\mathcal B}\colon\Mod_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal D)\to\Mod_{S\mathcal B}(\mathcal C),
$$
which commutes with the forgetful functors.

proof.text:
Write $m^S_{L,L'}=\delta_{L,L'}^{-1}$ and $e^S=\epsilon^{-1}$ for the strong monoidal structure maps. By the monoid-transport clause of [def-sfb-modobj-transport] applied to $S$, the monoid $S\mathcal B$ has multiplication $S(\mu_{\mathcal B})\circ m^S_{\mathcal B,\mathcal B}$ and unit $S(\eta_{\mathcal B})\circ e^S$. For $h:X\to GY$, write $T(h)=c_Y\circ P(h)$ for its transpose. This is the inverse of the hom-bijection of the assumed adjunction; thus it is injective and satisfies $T(G(v)\circ h\circ u)=v\circ T(h)\circ P(u)$, by functoriality and counit naturality. The defining equation of the mate is
$$T(\theta_{L,N})=(1_L\otimes c_N)\circ\pi_{L,GN}=:q_{L,N}.$$
We use these formulas to check the required identities directly.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: notation for transposition; second paragraph: the coefficient monoid

proof.text:
For $u:L\to L'$, the transposes of $G(u\otimes1_N)\circ\theta_{L,N}$ and $\theta_{L',N}\circ(Su\otimes1_{GN})$ are, respectively,
$$(u\otimes1_N)\circ(1_L\otimes c_N)\circ\pi_{L,GN},\qquad
(1_{L'}\otimes c_N)\circ\pi_{L',GN}\circ P(Su\otimes1_{GN}).$$
They agree by naturality of $\pi$ in $L$ and bifunctoriality of tensor. For $v:N\to N'$, the transposes of $G(1_L\otimes v)\circ\theta_{L,N}$ and $\theta_{L,N'}\circ(1_{SL}\otimes Gv)$ are
$$(1_L\otimes(v\circ c_N))\circ\pi_{L,GN},\qquad
(1_L\otimes(c_{N'}\circ PGv))\circ\pi_{L,GN},$$
where the second expression uses naturality of $\pi$ in its second variable. These agree by counit naturality. Injectivity of $T$ proves naturality of $\theta$ in both variables.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph, first bullet: naturality of the mate

proof.text:
The transpose of $G(\lambda_N)\circ\theta_{\mathbf1,N}\circ(e^S\otimes1_{GN})$ is
$$\begin{aligned}
\lambda_N\circ(1_{\mathbf1}\otimes c_N)\circ\pi_{\mathbf1,GN}\circ P(e^S\otimes1_{GN})
&=c_N\circ\lambda_{PGN}\circ\pi_{\mathbf1,GN}\circ P(e^S\otimes1_{GN})\\
&=c_N\circ P(\lambda_{GN}\circ(\epsilon\otimes1_{GN})\circ(e^S\otimes1_{GN}))\\
&=c_N\circ P(\lambda_{GN}).
\end{aligned}$$
The first equality is naturality of the unitor; the second is exactly the unit compatibility in [def-sfb-projection-formula]; the third uses $\epsilon e^S=1$. The last expression is $T(\lambda_{GN})$. Hence
$$G(\lambda_N)\circ\theta_{\mathbf1,N}\circ(e^S\otimes1_{GN})=\lambda_{GN}.$$

source.place: Proof, first paragraph, second bullet: unit identity of the mate

proof.text:
The transpose of
$$G(\alpha_{L,L',N})\circ\theta_{L\otimes L',N}\circ(m^S_{L,L'}\otimes1_{GN})$$
is
$$\alpha_{L,L',N}\circ(1_{L\otimes L'}\otimes c_N)\circ\pi_{L\otimes L',GN}\circ P(m^S_{L,L'}\otimes1_{GN}).$$
Naturality of the associator moves $c_N$ past $\alpha$. Apply the associativity compatibility of [def-sfb-projection-formula] at $M=GN$ and cancel $\delta_{L,L'}m^S_{L,L'}=1$. The result is
$$R=(1_L\otimes q_{L',N})\circ\pi_{L,SL'\otimes GN}\circ P(\alpha_{SL,SL',GN}).$$
On the other hand, the transpose of
$$\theta_{L,L'\otimes N}\circ(1_{SL}\otimes\theta_{L',N})\circ\alpha_{SL,SL',GN}$$
is
$$(1_L\otimes c_{L'\otimes N})\circ\pi_{L,G(L'\otimes N)}\circ P(1_{SL}\otimes\theta_{L',N})\circ P(\alpha_{SL,SL',GN}).$$
Naturality of $\pi$ at the morphism $\theta_{L',N}$ rewrites this as
$$(1_L\otimes(c_{L'\otimes N}\circ P\theta_{L',N}))\circ\pi_{L,SL'\otimes GN}\circ P(\alpha_{SL,SL',GN})=R,$$
using $T(\theta_{L',N})=q_{L',N}$. Injectivity of $T$ proves the claimed associativity identity for $\theta$.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph, third bullet: associativity identity of the mate

proof.text:
For a $\mathcal B$-module object $N$, put $a_N=G(\gamma_N)\circ\theta_{\mathcal B,N}$, and write $\eta$ and $\mu$ for the unit and multiplication of $\mathcal B$. The transported monoid formulas of Step 1, the first-variable naturality from Step 2, the module equations in [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], and Steps 3 and 4 give
$$\begin{aligned}
a_N\circ(\eta^{S\mathcal B}\otimes1_{GN})
&=G(\gamma_N\circ(\eta\otimes1_N))\circ\theta_{\mathbf1,N}\circ(e^S\otimes1_{GN})\\
&=G(\lambda_N)\circ\theta_{\mathbf1,N}\circ(e^S\otimes1_{GN})=\lambda_{GN},\\
a_N\circ(\mu^{S\mathcal B}\otimes1_{GN})
&=G(\gamma_N\circ(\mu\otimes1_N))\circ\theta_{\mathcal B\otimes\mathcal B,N}\circ(m^S_{\mathcal B,\mathcal B}\otimes1_{GN})\\
&=G(\gamma_N)\circ G(1_{\mathcal B}\otimes\gamma_N)\circ G(\alpha_{\mathcal B,\mathcal B,N})\circ\theta_{\mathcal B\otimes\mathcal B,N}\circ(m^S_{\mathcal B,\mathcal B}\otimes1_{GN})\\
&=G(\gamma_N)\circ G(1_{\mathcal B}\otimes\gamma_N)\circ\theta_{\mathcal B,\mathcal B\otimes N}\circ(1_{S\mathcal B}\otimes\theta_{\mathcal B,N})\circ\alpha_{S\mathcal B,S\mathcal B,GN}\\
&=G(\gamma_N)\circ\theta_{\mathcal B,N}\circ(1_{S\mathcal B}\otimes G(\gamma_N))\circ(1_{S\mathcal B}\otimes\theta_{\mathcal B,N})\circ\alpha_{S\mathcal B,S\mathcal B,GN}\\
&=a_N\circ(1_{S\mathcal B}\otimes a_N)\circ\alpha_{S\mathcal B,S\mathcal B,GN}.
\end{aligned}$$
The penultimate equality uses second-variable naturality at $\gamma_N:\mathcal B\otimes N\to N$. These are precisely the two required module-object axioms.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: verify both module axioms

proof.text:
For a $\mathcal B$-linear map $f:N\to N'$, its defining equation in [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and Step 2 give
$$\begin{aligned}
Gf\circ a_N
&=G(f\circ\gamma_N)\circ\theta_{\mathcal B,N}\\
&=G(\gamma_{N'})\circ G(1_{\mathcal B}\otimes f)\circ\theta_{\mathcal B,N}\\
&=G(\gamma_{N'})\circ\theta_{\mathcal B,N'}\circ(1_{S\mathcal B}\otimes Gf)
=a_{N'}\circ(1_{S\mathcal B}\otimes Gf).
\end{aligned}$$
Thus $Gf$ is linear. Define $G_{\mathcal B}$ by $(N,\gamma_N)\mapsto(GN,a_N)$ and $f\mapsto Gf$. The identity and composition laws hold because they hold for $G$ and module morphisms are underlying morphisms satisfying the displayed equation. Writing $U_{\mathcal B}$ and $U_{S\mathcal B}$ for the forgetful functors, both composites $U_{S\mathcal B}\circ G_{\mathcal B}$ and $G\circ U_{\mathcal B}$ send $N$ to $GN$ and $f$ to $Gf$; hence they agree.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: linearity, functor laws, and forgetful compatibility
